clue.text: Wild animal best caged initially when on board

indicators.note: to be 'on board' is to be inside the vessel, so the letters go inside the boat

parts.note: what one boards here is a BOAT

indicators.note: initially tells us to take the opening letters of best and caged

explanation.surface: A fierce creature is shut in a cage aboard ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when' is a link. 'on board' means aboard, so the initials go inside the vessel; 'board' suggests the craft you board.
explanation.definitionFit: The bobcat is a North American lynx, a wild member of the cat family.

clue.text: See 12
Account on "Cristo" with bad write up? That's puzzling

indicators.note: bad suggests the letters of Cristo are spoiled and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone reviews a poor write-up of The Count of Monte Cristo, finding it baffling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' and 'with' are links. The definition reads oddly: an acrostic is a written-up word puzzle.
explanation.definitionFit: An acrostic is a composition whose initial letters spell a word, so it is a written puzzle.

clue.text: Dry rot returns in a certain area

parts.note: sec is the wine term for dry

indicators.note: returns tells us the word rot is read backwards

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Dry rot keeps recurring in one particular part of a building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returns' turns ROT into TOR; 'in' is a link to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A sector is a distinct zone or part of a larger region.

clue.text: Is it unlikely to be painted by Landseer?

definitions.text: Is it unlikely to be painted by Landseer?

parts.words: Is it unlikely to be painted by Landseer?
parts.note: Sir Edwin Landseer, a Victorian British painter of animals, is read as a Land-seer, one who looks at land rather than the sea

explanation.surface: A question about which subjects a famous Victorian animal painter would avoid.
explanation.definitionFit: A seascape depicts the ocean, the opposite of what a 'land seer' would paint.

clue.text: Study panel member: he's possibly in the Circle

parts.note: to con is an old word for to study or learn
a juror is a member of a jury panel

explanation.surface: A member of a study panel might belong to some exclusive circle.
explanation.walkthrough: The Circle is the Magic Circle, the London society of magicians.
explanation.definitionFit: A magician or illusionist might well be a member of the Magic Circle.

clue.text: Range of opinions, very colourful

definitions.meaning: the full spread of views, from one extreme to the other
the rainbow band of every hue that light splits into

explanation.surface: A colourful variety of views.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a span of views and the band of colours from split light share this name.

clue.text: Authentic old coin

definitions.meaning: a former silver coin of Spain

explanation.surface: A genuine antique coin.
explanation.definitionFit: Means genuine, and was also the name of a historic Spanish currency unit.

clue.text: The air of one amongst the people

indicators.note: amongst places the numeral among the letters for people

parts.note: people as men
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A single person's bearing stands out in a crowd.
explanation.definitionFit: An air in the sense of bearing or manner is a person's look or demeanour.

clue.text: What helps with bruises? Fresh air can

indicators.note: fresh suggests a new arrangement of the letters of air can

explanation.surface: Some fresh air might help soothe bruising.
explanation.definitionFit: Arnica is a herbal remedy traditionally applied to bruises and sprains.

clue.text: Company youth going in top honour

indicators.note: going in places the company and youth inside the word for top

parts.note: ace means first-rate, top
a lad is a youth

explanation.surface: A firm's young apprentice wins the highest award.
explanation.definitionFit: An accolade is an award or expression of praise, an honour.

clue.text: Bit of a token match

parts.note: a counter is a token used in games
a part is a bit

explanation.surface: A small piece of a token used to strike a match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of a' joins the pieces; the bit comes after the token in the answer, though the clue names it first.
explanation.definitionFit: A counterpart is an equivalent, something that matches another.

clue.text: For seeing things in the best light?

definitions.text: For seeing things in the best light?

parts.words: For seeing things in the best light?
parts.note: describes glasses with a pink tint, worn figuratively by optimists who view everything favourably

explanation.surface: Something that lets you see the world at its most flattering.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes an overly optimistic view, as if through pink-tinged glasses.

clue.text: It's supporting judge and university member to act quickly

indicators.note: in a down clue, a piece supporting others sits beneath them, at the end

parts.note: MP is a Member of Parliament
taken as written
the 's is the verb 'is', so only the word it gives letters

explanation.surface: A support for a judge and a university member urging swift action.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supporting' puts IT at the foot of the down entry, under J, U, MP and TO.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to get on with something promptly and energetically.

clue.text: Yes, lamb's being cooked for the multitude

indicators.note: cooked suggests the letters of yes and lambs are worked over and rearranged

parts.note: the 's here counts as an S, giving lambs

explanation.surface: Lamb is roasting to feed a big crowd.
explanation.definitionFit: An assembly is a gathering of many people, a crowd or multitude.

clue.text: Foreign Office backed in media claim

indicators.note: in places the backed letters inside the word for media

parts.note: the press is the news media

indicators.note: backed tells us the abbreviation is read in reverse

explanation.surface: The Foreign Office is backed by press reports in making a claim.
explanation.definitionFit: To profess is to declare or claim, often falsely.

clue.text: Swap the old collection of coins

parts.note: ex is a former one, as in an ex-partner
change is loose coins

explanation.surface: Trading in an old coin collection.
explanation.definitionFit: To exchange is to trade one thing for another, to swap.

clue.text: Capsule incorrectly programmed for supporters at ground level

indicators.note: a wrongly programmed sequence muddles the letters of capsule

explanation.surface: A space capsule wrongly programmed lands its crew at ground level.
explanation.definitionFit: Lace-up shoes support the feet and sit at the very bottom of a person.

clue.text: Reserves among players right to hope trouble's a disaster?

indicators.note: among puts the reserves inside the word for players

parts.note: the cast are the players in a show
TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve force

indicators.note: trouble suggests the letters of hope are disturbed and rearranged

explanation.surface: Reserve players and a hope of a comeback collapse into disaster for the team.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trouble's' rearranges HOPE into OPHE; 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A catastrophe is a sudden great misfortune, a disaster.

clue.text: One in comeback for a second game

indicators.note: in places the single letter inside the comeback

parts.note: a reply is a retort, a comeback
A is one, as in 'a'

explanation.surface: A team makes a comeback to force a second match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for a' joins wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A replay is a match played again, as when a cup tie is drawn.

clue.text: Insects not the first in the tree

indicators.note: not the first removes the opening letter of the word for insects

parts.note: pupas are insects in their pupal stage

explanation.surface: Insects other than the first ones live in the tree.
explanation.definitionFit: The upas is a Javanese tree with poisonous sap.

clue.text: Head covering it up outside work

indicators.note: outside puts the reversed word around the work
up in a down clue turns the word it backwards

parts.note: OP is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: A hat lifted up outside the workplace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses in a down clue: the reversed word wraps round the work.
explanation.definitionFit: A topi is a lightweight sun helmet worn in hot countries.

clue.text: Opt for reform state producing decaying matter?

indicators.note: reform means to shape again, so the letters of opt are rearranged

parts.note: Maine is a US state

explanation.surface: Choosing state reform leaves things rotten.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reform' rearranges OPT into PTO; 'for' and 'producing' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Ptomaines are compounds formed in putrefying matter, so the term evokes decay.

clue.text: A place to ring doctor for assurance

parts.note: O is ring-shaped
MB is a Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor

explanation.surface: Someone wants a place where they can phone the doctor for reassurance.
explanation.definitionFit: Aplomb is self-assurance or poise.

clue.text: "No doubles for drunk" produces complaint

indicators.note: a drunk slurs the s sound into sh

parts.note: singles are not doubles, in tennis or drinks

explanation.surface: A barman refusing doubles to a drunk causes a complaint.
explanation.definitionFit: Shingles is a painful viral illness, a medical complaint.

clue.text: An officer comes in to snoop? That's mean!

indicators.note: comes in puts these letters into the word for snoop

parts.note: to pry is to snoop
A as written for an
LT is short for lieutenant, an officer

explanation.surface: An officer arrives to snoop; how mean.
explanation.definitionFit: Paltry means petty, trifling or mean.
